title: NAB eyes up HSBC deposit book
full_text:
NAB is suspected to be back around the hoop for a potential acquisition of HSBC’s Australian deposit book, after considering a deal to buy that part of the banking operation last year.
It comes after the London-based bank sold its $36bn Australian home and personal loan portfolio to Blackstone in July a deal that also brought in Pepper Money to manage the assets.
However, HSBC’s advisers now remain at work to clear the rest of the Australian retail business – namely its deposit book.
DataRoom understands that banks are around the hoop currently doing diligence on the operation.
It is believed that NAB put forward a non-conforming bid for HSBC last year that was understood to have involved a deal to buy just the deposits but not the loans.
Sources say the deposits were the most appealing part of the offering and that NAB is short of deposits. NAB acquired the Citi retail banking business in 2022 for $1.2bn. Citi has been working on the sale of HSBC.
The sale aligns with HSBC’s global strategy of prioritising its home markets of Hong Kong and the UK, while sharpening focus on Asian operations. Europe’s largest bank by assets has been systematically exiting non-core markets, selling its US retail operations in 2021, followed by a deal to offload Canadian operations to Royal Bank of Canada the following year. The Australian divestment would mark another significant retreat by a global bank from the local market. HSBC said in a statement earlier in the year that it would continue to invest in and grow its corporate and institutional banking, private banking and asset management businesses in Australia.
